title: Answers to Questions: The 21st Arab Summit, Gül's Visit to Iraq and the Kurdish Issue, Ahmed Sharif, President of Somalia, and the Mujahideen Youth Movement
text:
Answers to Questions:

The 21st Arab Summit,

Gül's Visit to Iraq and the Kurdish Issue,

Ahmed Sharif, President of Somalia, and the Mujahideen Youth Movement (al-Shabaab)

The First Question:

On Monday 30/3/2009 CE the twenty-first Arab summit conference was held, and instead of continuing for two days as had been scheduled, the conference completed its task on the same day. So what is behind this conference, and how effective are its resolutions?

Answer:

There is nothing behind this conference, and likewise no resolutions of any significance came out of it such that one might ask how effective they are. For the picture to become clearer, we mention the following:

1- The summit conferences have come to be held "routinely" in March of every year.

2- The major states have been accustomed to exploiting the Arab summit conferences for their projects relating to the issue of Palestine, which they called "the Middle East issue". The states influential in that at the beginnings of the summits in the sixties were America and Britain; then, when Britain's influence weakened after that, the force influential in these conferences and moving them became America.

3- In the recent period, America's circumstances have become shaken and turbulent, and it has priorities that come before the Middle East issue, especially since the economic crisis struck it, in addition to its predicament in Iraq and Afghanistan; thus it has concentrated its attention on these priorities.

4- For this reason, although Netanyahu declares openly that he does not want the two-state project that America calls for, and although America could have brought him down in the elections as it did previously, it left matters alone and did not occupy itself with them, and was content with having Barak share with him, as a face-saving measure for itself, that Netanyahu has not monopolised power completely but has with him one who calls for its project, namely Barak! At the same time it realises that the weakness of the votes he obtained will not enable him to prevent Netanyahu from proceeding with his views.

All this indicates that America has not placed on its agenda any solution to the issue, even a feeble one; that is, it has left matters to proceed in the region without serious intervention from it until it is free of its priorities or covers some distance in them, and after that it will turn towards "the Middle East issue". Then neither Netanyahu nor anyone else of the Jewish entity will be beyond it, especially as the life and death of the Jewish entity is in the hand of America. Until it covers some distance in its priorities, it has left the movement on the issue of Palestine to its loyal follower Hosni Mubarak, to fill the vacuum as required, and not to a conference with which it does not want to occupy itself at the present time... During that, it sends a delegate or envoy of its own to monitor the ongoing reality and gather information until the time comes for the "turn" of the Middle East issue, after America has covered some distance in its priorities.

5- For this reason, America left this conference to proceed in a routine manner; that is, the Arab rulers met, ate, drank, smiled at one another and "needled" one another, and spoke about reconciliation with loose talk open to more than one interpretation...

Therefore the most that can be said in describing this conference is that it is a public relations conference between the Arab rulers... until America completes its priorities or covers some distance in them; after that, large and small conferences may be held, moved by America, to take decisions that serve its interests.

The Second Question:

On 23/3/2009, the president of the republic of Turkey, Abdullah Gül, made a visit to Iraq which lasted two days. It is the first visit by a Turkish president of the republic in 33 years. He met with the president of the republic, Talabani, and the prime minister, al-Maliki, and also with Nechirvan Barzani, prime minister of the Kurdistan Region, which made the latter declare: "The Turkish president's meeting with him is a recognition on Turkey's part of the Kurdistan Region." (25/3/2009, Turkish news television). Talabani also declared at a press conference with the Turkish president: "The Kurdistan Workers' Party must lay down their arms or leave." (Radio Sawa 23/3/2009). Does this mean that the presence of the Turkish Kurdistan Workers' Party in Iraq has ended, in return for a Turkish recognition of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, but within the state of Iraq? And consequently, have the Kurds of Iraq despaired of America's promises to them of a state independent of Iraq? Then, does the visit have an international dimension, or is it within the limits of the relationship between Iraq and Turkey?

Answer:

1- Yes, America's promises to the Kurds of Iraq of establishing a state for them were never serious promises; rather, it promised them that in order to exploit them to strike their brothers in Iraq, so as to facilitate the occupation of Iraq. Just as Britain promised Mahmud al-Hafid in 1919 that he would attack the Ottoman garrison in Sulaymaniyah in return for the promise of a Kurdish state; so they attacked it and killed their Ottoman brothers in the garrison and expelled those of them who survived; then Britain broke its promise, and indeed exiled Mahmud al-Hafid to its colony, India. Likewise, Britain insisted in the Treaty of Sèvres in 1920 CE with the Ottoman state on placing a clause relating to the establishment of a Kurdish state, in order to disturb the Khalifah Mehmed Vahideddin, as the Khalifah's delegation was the negotiator. Then, when it later succeeded in installing Mustafa Kemal as president of the republic and the Khilafah ended, and the treaty came to be with the republic of Mustafa Kemal at Lausanne in 1924, Britain refused to place the clause on the Kurdish state, because it had achieved its goal, namely bringing down the Khilafah, so exploiting such a thing was no longer necessary. Britain used to stir up the feelings of Kurdish nationalist chauvinism and stir up the feelings of all the nationalist chauvinisms in the region, and exploit those whom it stirred up and incited to disobedience and rebellion against the Islamic State until it achieved its purposes; then it would spit out those who cooperated with it, or harness them as its agents when it installed them as so-called rulers and leaders. Then America came and performed the same role and played the same game, and did with those cooperating with it the same thing, that is, mere promises which it exploits to serve its interests, until when its interests are achieved its promises are gone as though they had never existed the day before!

2- It is not unlikely that Turkey will officially recognise the Kurdistan Region, but within the state of Iraq, without a state of their own, on condition of expelling the Kurdistan Workers' Party. Abdullah Gül declared to journalists following his meeting with Nechirvan Barzani: "I informed him frankly that the terrorist organisation of the Kurdistan Workers' Party and its camps are in your region. So you must take a clear position against it. And when it is eliminated, everything between us and you is possible. For you are our neighbours and our relatives." (Reuters 25/3/2009). Gül had met with Talabani on 17/3/2009 in Istanbul on the sidelines of the meetings of the Fifth World Water Forum, and declared from there the impossibility of establishing the Kurdish state, and that the Kurdish state exists only in Kurdish poems. And he demanded that the Kurdistan Workers' Party lay down its arms.

It appears that the rulers of the Kurdistan Region want to respond to Turkey's demands in return for Turkey's recognition of them. Nechirvan Barzani said: "We want the relationship with Turkey to be good, and we understand Turkey's fears." (The American CNN 25/3/2009) And he added: "We do not accept attacks on the neighbouring countries from Iraq or from the Kurdistan region." (The American CNN 25/3/2009). It was recently announced by sources in the Turkish foreign ministry that Turkey has accepted the request of the president of the Kurdistan Region, Masoud Barzani, to visit Ankara (CNN 26/3/2009). This visit relates to the same subject, namely expelling the Kurdistan Workers' Party from the Kurdistan Region in return for Turkey's recognition of the region within the state of Iraq; this, even though the presence of the Kurdistan Workers' Party in the north of Iraq was under the cover of Barzani's party, the "Kurdistan Democratic Party"!!

3- Besides that, Gül's visit also touched on the settlement of the question of Kirkuk; Turkey rejects the annexation of Kirkuk to the Kurdistan Region. Abdullah Gül met with representatives of the Turkmen and affirmed to them that Turkey rejects the annexation of Kirkuk to any party. He did not concentrate on it because it comes in second place for Turkey; and on the other hand Turkey knows that there are great obstacles preventing the annexation of Kirkuk to Kurdistan, and Turkey is one of these obstacles.

There are other questions that were discussed, such as the transport of oil through Turkey, trade, and increasing the quantity of water, and the two sides showed that they are in agreement on them.

4- As for whether the visit has an international dimension: yes, and it is the most important. The visit of the president of the republic of Turkey to Iraq comes after the decision of the Americans concerning the gradual withdrawal of their forces from Iraq, except for the sensitive centres, and America wants states loyal to it to perform the role in its place, so that another major state does not come and exploit the situation and take America's place, or work to disrupt its influence.

From here came the role of Iran in coordination with America, which agreed with it upon it, and that was crowned by the visit of the president of the republic of Iran to Baghdad last year. But America does not want to rely on one state, for one state may be able to perform a certain role, but it cannot do everything that America demands of it. Therefore America wants a role likewise for Turkey and Syria... From here came Gül's visit to Iraq, and following Gül's visit, the foreign minister of Syria visited Iraq and met with Talabani. America cannot achieve everything it wants in isolation from the neighbouring states. This applies to every country. So we see it seeking the help of Pakistan and Iran, the neighbours of Afghanistan, in achieving its goals in Afghanistan; it even seeks the help of states in which its influence is mixed with the influence of the English, such as Saudi Arabia, to influence the mujahideen there to accept negotiation. The Hague conference held yesterday, 31/3/2009 CE, regarding Afghanistan is the strongest witness to that, as about seventy states attended it, and among the most prominent attendees was Iran, the head of whose delegation met with the American envoy for Afghanistan, and the meeting was described as having been friendly...!

America wants to preserve its influence in Iraq and its standing as the first major state in the world, after it tasted the bitterness of the defeats that befell it there at the hands of those resisting it, which almost lowered its international standing and dislodged it from its position as the first state in the world. Nevertheless, confidence in it as the first major state in the world, which used to claim that it does what it wants, has been shaken!

For this reason, Obama's message to Turkey was that America wants to seek Turkey's help. America's seeking the help of Turkey, or more correctly America's use of Turkey, is not only with regard to the Iraqi situation; rather, there are several issues in which America wants to use Turkey, such as the issue of the Caucasus countries and Russia, and the Middle East issue. For this reason the new president of America, Obama, announced that he will visit Turkey soon. Obama had also directed another message to Iran, in order to seek its help, indeed to use it, in the issue of Afghanistan alongside the issue of Iraq.

The Third Question:

Sheikh Sharif Ahmed has become president of Somalia. Does that mean that the Islamic Courts have returned to Somalia as they were two years ago? And if the matter is so, why then does the Mujahideen Youth Movement stand against it, when it was part of the Courts or close to them? And if Sheikh Sharif has changed, and the Mujahideen Youth Movement has stood against him because of his deviation, does that mean that the Mujahideen Youth Movement is a truthful, sincere movement?

Answer:

Yes, Sheikh Sharif Ahmed today is not like him yesterday. When he was previously head of the Islamic Courts and reached power in Somalia, he was at that time fighting the foreign ambitions in Somalia of the Kafir colonialists, and speaking of applying the Islamic Sharia. But political awareness was weak in him, as is the case with most of the armed Islamic movements. Therefore "the sincere" sent him a delegation advising him not to negotiate with the government of Abdullahi Yusuf, for it is subordinate to America, and not to negotiate with America, neither directly nor indirectly by way of its agents or under the shadow of the United Nations, the Arab League or the African Union... for in all of that, the fingers of America, indeed its hands, are not absent from meddling in it and moving it. The delegation also advised him to continue his hostility to the Kafir colonialists... However, he did not take the advice as it should be taken; rather, he negotiated with the government of Abdullahi Yusuf in Khartoum and under the shadow of the United Nations, the Arab League and the African Union...

This was while he was in power. As for after the Ethiopian invasion and Sharif's departure from Somalia to Kenya, and after that he reached Djibouti and became head of the Alliance for the Re-liberation of Somalia, the Djibouti wing, after the Islamic Courts split among themselves and the two settled in Asmara and Djibouti, even though the two states are loyal to the West...! During that, Sheikh Sharif immersed himself in direct and indirect negotiations, until matters reached the point of him heading a government in Somalia that does not differ much from the government of Abdullahi Yusuf, with the blessing of America, the West and the agents... Matters proceeded as follows:

1- After Sheikh Sharif's departure from Somalia following the defeat of the Islamic Courts at the end of 2006 CE before the Ethiopian forces, which America pushed to invade Somalia on its behalf, when he went out to Kenya he met with the American ambassador in Kenya in the presence of officials of the American Central Intelligence Agency.

2- After the Courts split among themselves and came to have two wings, Sheikh Sharif Ahmed headed the Djibouti wing, and negotiations began between him and the government of Abdullahi Yusuf and Ethiopia, until the Djibouti agreement was concluded on 26/10/2008 CE.

3- The agreement came under American sponsorship and with Ethiopian approval, because the Ethiopian army had suffered several losses and wanted to leave, but with saving face, that is, by an agreement stipulating that. For this reason, after the signing of the agreement, Ethiopia began issuing statements about withdrawing its forces.

The agency France-Presse (AFP) reported on 28/11/2008 that Ethiopia will withdraw from Somalia by the end of the year, in two official letters to the African Union and to the United Nations. This agency said that Wahide Belay, the spokesman for the Ethiopian foreign ministry, told it: "We have reached the conclusion that it is not appropriate for Ethiopia to keep its forces in Somalia. We have done our job and we are proud of that, but the hopes we placed in the international community have been disappointed." This Ethiopian spokesman had earlier commented on 24/11/2008 to the same agency on the agreement in Djibouti, saying: "It flows in the direction of Ethiopia's position and the orderly withdrawal of its forces."

The matter of Somalia is of concern to Ethiopia, not only as a proxy fighter for the benefit of America, but because it is its neighbour and occupies the Somali region of Ogaden, for which Somalia fought a war with Ethiopia in 1977 and 1978 to recover it, but it failed. Ethiopia wants there to be in Somalia a government that does not threaten it and does not demand Ogaden from it; this is in addition to Ethiopia's service of America's interests in the Horn of Africa. It is America that sent Ethiopia into Somalia, and it is America that asked it to withdraw after the Djibouti agreement of 26/10/2008 CE, when it found what it was looking for in Sheikh Sharif.

4- America saw that Sheikh Sharif is the most capable of confronting the mujahideen, because he has an Islamic background, and Ethiopia, as an African state, cannot continue to fight the Islamists. So it was better for America to use one of the Islamists to perform this role. America set its agents in Kenya and Sudan upon Sharif to win him over, especially Sudan. The political expert Hassan Makki says: "The Sudanese government told Sharif that he cannot bypass the Ethiopians, and he cannot deal with the international community as if it does not exist; therefore he began to listen to this advice, especially as he is a graduate of Sudanese educational institutions." And he adds: "The Sudanese mediator played a great role in these reconciliations", meaning in the Djibouti talks.

Thus America succeeded in winning over Sheikh Sharif, to the extent that he began praising it. In an interview with "Voice of America, Somali section" on 20/2/2009, he described American policy towards Somalia as positive from the start of the negotiations until now. And he said: "We hope it will continue those efforts."!

5- After Sheikh Sharif became president of Somalia by a majority of votes of the parliament that existed in the era of Abdullahi Yusuf! the next step was the choice of the prime minister. And here too came America's role, as Omar Abdirashid Sharmarke was chosen, who was residing in the United States. He is described as moderate according to the standards of the United States, he has held several posts in the United Nations, he was ambassador of Somalia in Washington in the era of the government of Abdullahi Yusuf, and he is the son of a former Somali president.

America was keen on his assuming the premiership because of his previous residence in America, and also because he was not tainted by the civil war, as he was far from it and from his country; therefore he had a kind of acceptance among the general people in Somalia.

It is worth mentioning that, as is the custom of the colonialist states, if they find their interest with a man other than the man who is currently serving them, they spit him out as one spits out a date stone and bring the other who achieves their interests with better ability. So America abandoned Abdullahi Yusuf, who had become burnt out, hated and exposed in his treachery to Somalia, so he was compelled to resign on 29/12/2008 CE and to depart from Mogadishu to his birthplace, Puntland, which is the region he ruled from 1998 CE until 2004, when he was declared president of Somalia; then he later took refuge in Yemen...

7- America thought that by its success in bringing Sheikh Sharif to the presidency of the state, he being of the Islamic background in the Courts, which had a public opinion during their rule, and likewise by the arrival of a prime minister who had been far from the civil war, which gives him acceptance among the general people, it thought that by this it had succeeded in taking hold of Somalia. However, its expectation was disappointed by the exposure of the matter of the new government in Somalia, as it became clear that this government does not differ much from the previous one, except that it wears a garment more adorned and beautiful than the garment of the previous government.

The difference between the two governments, if we think well of them, is that Abdullahi Yusuf was serving America knowingly, and Sheikh Sharif is serving America out of ignorance, while he thinks that he is doing good to Somalia! We would have loved for Sheikh Sharif to remain as he began, far from the conspiracies of the Kafir colonialists, and perhaps he will return to his first course, by the permission of Allah.

8- In the light of what has been exposed of the matter of this government, the resistance of the Muslims has continued at its most intense, and among its most prominent is the Mujahideen Youth Movement.

The Mujahideen Youth Movement separated from the Islamic Courts, the Asmara wing and the Djibouti wing, after the two signed the Asmara agreement in September 2007 CE, as it accused them of having allied with the secularists and abandoned Jihad in the way of Allah...

It declares that it wants Jihad against Ethiopia and against America to liberate the entire region of the Horn of Africa, and it also wants to establish an Islamic rule that transcends the narrow patriotisms... The American State Department issued a statement in which it declares that the Shabaab movement is an extremist and violent group, a number of whose members belong to the al-Qaeda organisation (the Chinese People's page 18/3/2008). The United States had arrested in mid-2007 its former leader Ismail Arale, and that was in Djibouti, and placed him in the Guantanamo detention camp. The movement chose Mukhtar Abdirahman "Abu Zubeyr" as its leader and Mukhtar Robow "Abu Mansur" as its official spokesman (Al Arabiya 22/12/2007). This official spokesman responded to the American State Department by saying: "Our relationship with al-Qaeda is the relationship of the Muslim with his Muslim brother, and from the core of the Muslim's creed is (al-wala' wal-bara', loyalty and disavowal) and (that we keep away from the Kafirs and that we join with all the Muslims and love them)." And he said that the movement "was pleased and is proud of the decision of the United States of America to place it on the terrorism list." And it came in a statement issued by the movement on 5/4/2008 CE: "We know with certain knowledge that we have not been targeted because we are Somalis, but because we carry the thought of Jihad in its general concept, which does not recognise the illusory borders nor what is called (international legitimacy)."

The Mujahideen Youth Movement has succeeded in controlling many Somali cities, far exceeding the control of the government. What appears from this movement is that it fights the Kafir colonialists with truthfulness and sincerity... However, the point of weakness, as we mentioned, in the armed Islamic movements is the weakness of political awareness, and we ask Allah (swt) for this movement to continue in its strong position against the Kafir colonialists.

Nevertheless, it is more aware than the Islamic Party (Hizbul Islam), which likewise opposes the government of Sheikh Sharif. It is made up of four movements, the most prominent of which is the Alliance for the Re-liberation of Somalia, the Asmara wing, led by Hassan Dahir Aweys; the other three movements in the Islamic Party are the Ras Kamboni camp, the Islamic Front, and the Faruq camp. The page "Gerinj site" on 24/1/2009 CE, which is a page close to the Mujahideen Youth Movement, asked Hassan Dahir Aweys about the reason for his presence in the Eritrean capital Asmara, and he answered: these have become for us as the Najashi was for the first Muslims!! This is what he says!!

We ask Allah (swt) for the Islamic movements sincerity to Allah (swt), truthfulness with the Messenger of Allah (saw), and complete awareness of the plans of the Kafirs and their conspiracies, for they plot against Islam and harbour evil for it beyond what they declare: "Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." Whoever relies upon them loses his world and his Hereafter, and that is the manifest loss, and the witnesses of that are many and widespread...
